You are writing or repairing Structurizr DSL — the text format for C4
architecture workspaces. The workspace is a single file (in practice

## The authoring rules

The rules whose violations surface as parse errors, missing model facts,
or misleading diagrams. The full reference is `references/gotchas.md`
with the exact error strings; the short list:

1. **Declare elements before the relationships that use them.** The DSL
   is parsed top to bottom, so a forward reference fails with
   `The destination element "x" does not exist` — the same error as a
   typo. Check the identifier first, then the order.
2. **Quote every value that contains spaces** — names, descriptions,
   technologies, custom-element metadata. Quotes are optional only for a
   single token; an unquoted phrase with more tokens than the statement
   has left over fails with `Too many tokens, expected: ...`. To skip an
   optional property you want to leave empty, use `""`.
3. **Braces:** the opening `{` sits on the same line as the statement;
   the closing `}` sits on a line of its own.
4. **Identifiers are flat and unique** across the whole workspace by
   default (characters `a-zA-Z_0-9`); a second declaration of the same
   identifier fails with `The identifier "x" is already in use`. Rename
   it — do not delete the element.
5. **Every relationship gets a description and a technology:**
   `a -> b "Reads orders from" "HTTPS/JSON"`. Between the same pair, the
   description is the relationship's identity — two relationships with
   the same description are a duplicate.
6. **Every element gets a description** (a custom `element`'s second
   string is its metadata).
7. **Give every view an explicit key** (characters `a-zA-Z0-9_-`, no
   spaces).

  elements (person, softwareSystem, container, component, group, custom
  `element`), relationships and their uniqueness, identifiers (flat and
  hierarchical), constants and variables.

  container, component, dynamic, deployment, filtered), include/exclude
  expressions, styles and the standard C4 recipe, themes, terminology,
  configuration, and the small pattern set.
- `references/gotchas.md` — the error table and the rule behind each
  error, declaration order, implied relationships, and the MCP notes.

not validate is not done. Your host prefixes the MCP tool names (for
example `structurizr_validate`; the in-harness server name is
`structurizr`), so call whichever prefixed variant your host exposes. The
full parse/validate/inspect loop with finding triage is the
`structurizr-validate-loop` skill's task — that skill is for validating a
model, not for authoring its text.

7: passage-by-passage mapping.
8: 
9: ## Syntax fundamentals
10: 
11: - Lines are processed **sequentially** — no forward references
12: - Keywords are **case-insensitive** (`softwareSystem` = `softwaresystem`)
13: - Double quotes are optional for single-word values without spaces
14: - Opening `{` must be on the **same line** as the statement
15: - Closing `}` must be on its **own line**
16: - Opening/closing braces are only required when adding child content
17: - Use `""` as a placeholder for an earlier optional property that you
18:   want to skip (for example `person "Name" "" "Tag"` — no description,
19:   but a tag)
20: - Tags are comma separated (`"Tag 1,Tag 2,Tag 3"`)
21: - Comments: `//` or `#` (single-line), `/* ... */` (multi-line)
22: - Line continuation: `\` as the last character on the line
23: - Identifier characters: `a-zA-Z_0-9`
24: 
25: ### Constants and Variables
26: 
27: ```dsl
28: !const SYSTEM_NAME "My System"        # immutable
29: !var VERSION "1.0"                    # redefinable
30: # Reference: ${SYSTEM_NAME}, ${VERSION}
31: ```
32: 
33: Constant and variable names may only contain `a-zA-Z0-9-_.`. String
34: substitution runs on any token written as `${NAME}`, where `NAME` is a
35: constant, a variable, or an environment variable; a name that cannot be
36: found is left unsubstituted.
37: 
38: ## Workspace structure
39: 
40: ```dsl
41: workspace [name] [description] {
42:     !identifiers hierarchical          # recommended for non-trivial models
43:     !impliedRelationships true         # default: auto-creates parent relationships
44: 
45:     model {
46:         # people, systems, relationships
47:     }
48: 
49:     views {
50:         # diagram definitions, styles, themes
51:     }
52: 
53:     configuration {
54:         # scope, visibility, users
55:     }
56: }
57: ```
58: 
59: ## Model elements
60: 
61: By default every element is **anonymous** — it cannot be referenced from
62: the DSL. Give an element an identifier where you plan to reference it
63: (relationships, view include/exclude, ...): `p = person "User"`.
64: 
65: ### Person
66: 
67: ```dsl
68: <id> = person <name> [description] [tags]
69: # or with block:
70: <id> = person <name> [description] [tags] {
71:     description "..."
72:     tags "Tag1" "Tag2"
73:     url "https://..."
74:     properties { key value }
75:     -> <target> [description] [technology] [tags]
76: }
77: ```
78: 
79: Default tags: `Element`, `Person`
80: 
81: ### Software System
82: 
83: ```dsl
84: <id> = softwareSystem <name> [description] [tags] {
85:     group <name> { ... }
86:     <id> = container <name> [description] [technology] [tags] { ... }
87:     -> <target> [description] [technology] [tags]
88: }
89: ```
90: 
91: Default tags: `Element`, `Software System`
92: 
93: ### Container
94: 
95: ```dsl
96: <id> = container <name> [description] [technology] [tags] {
97:     group <name> { ... }
98:     <id> = component <name> [description] [technology] [tags] { ... }
99:     -> <target> [description] [technology] [tags]
100: }
101: ```
102: 
103: Default tags: `Element`, `Container`
104: 
105: ### Component
106: 
107: ```dsl
108: <id> = component <name> [description] [technology] [tags] {
109:     description "..."
110:     technology "..."
111:     tags "..."
112:     -> <target> [description] [technology] [tags]
113: }
114: ```
115: 
116: Default tags: `Element`, `Component`
117:

120: The `element` keyword defines a custom element that sits outside of the
121: C4 model — hardware, a third-party feed, anything that is not a person,
122: system, container or component:
123: 
124: ```dsl
125: <id> = element <name> [metadata] [description] [tags]
126: ```
127: 
128: Default tags: `Element`. In the exported model the first optional string
129: is the element's **metadata** — when in doubt, put the human description
130: there.
131: 
132: ### Group
133: 
134: ```dsl
135: group <name> {
136:     # elements of the same type
137: }
138: ```
139:

144:     properties {
145:         "structurizr.groupSeparator" "/"

151:     }
152: }
153: ```

178: identifier: `rel = p -> ss "Uses"`.

200: system fails with `The identifier "api" is already in use`.

214: }

216: ```
217:

1: # Views, styles and patterns
2: 
3: The view, style, theme and configuration syntax of `workspace.dsl`.
4: Adapted from the `structurizr-dsl` skill of `jrjsmrtn/c4-skills` (MIT,
5: see `NOTICE.md`); see `source-map.md` for the passage-by-passage
6: mapping.
7: 
8: ## Views
9: 
10: Every view should carry an **explicit key** (characters `a-zA-Z0-9_-`,
11: no spaces) — a view without a key gets an auto-generated one that is not
12: guaranteed to be stable over time, and you will likely lose manual
13: layout information.
14: 
15: ### System Landscape
16: 
17: ```dsl
18: systemLandscape [key] [description] {
19:     include *
20:     autoLayout [tb|bt|lr|rl] [rankSep] [nodeSep]
21:     title "Title"
22:     description "..."
23: }
24: ```
25: 
26: ### System Context
27: 
28: ```dsl
29: systemContext <systemId> [key] [description] {
30:     include *
31:     autoLayout
32:     title "System Context for X"
33: }
34: ```
35: 
36: ### Container View
37: 
38: ```dsl
39: container <systemId> [key] [description] {
40:     include *
41:     autoLayout
42:     title "Containers for X"
43: }
44: ```
45: 
46: ### Component View
47: 
48: ```dsl
49: component <containerId> [key] [description] {
50:     include *
51:     autoLayout
52:     title "Components of X"
53: }
54: ```
55: 
56: ### Dynamic View
57: 
58: ```dsl
59: dynamic <scope> [key] [description] {
60:     # scope: * (people/systems), systemId (+ containers), containerId (+ components)
61:     <source> -> <destination> [description] [technology]
62:     <source> -> <destination> [description] [technology]
63:     autoLayout
64:     title "Feature Y Flow"
65: }
66: ```
67: 
68: Interactions are automatically numbered in order. To set explicit
69: ordering:
70: 
71: ```dsl
72: dynamic <scope> [key] [description] {
73:     1: user -> system.api "submits order" "HTTPS"
74:     2: system.api -> system.db "persists order" "SQL"
75:     3: system.api -> system.queue "publishes event" "AMQP"
76: }
77: ```
78: 
79: ### Deployment View
80: 
81: ```dsl
82: deployment <systemId|*> <environment> [key] [description] {
83:     include *
84:     autoLayout
85:     title "Production Deployment"
86: }
87: ```
88: 
89: ### Filtered View
90: 
91: ```dsl
92: filtered <baseViewKey> <include|exclude> <tags> [key] [description]
93: ```
94: 
95: Creates a view on top of another, filtering elements by tags. The base
96: view is hidden when a filtered view exists.
97: 
98: ### AutoLayout
99: 
100: ```dsl
101: autoLayout [direction] [rankSeparation] [nodeSeparation]
102: # direction: tb (default), bt, lr, rl
103: # default separations: 300px each
104: ```
105: 
106: ### Include/Exclude with Expressions
107: 
108: Element expressions:
109: 
110: ```dsl
111: include element.type==Container
112: include element.tag==Database
113: include element.tag!=External
114: include element.parent==<id>
115: include element.technology==PostgreSQL
116: include ->system.api->                 # elements connected to system.api (both directions)
117: include ->system.api                   # elements that depend on system.api (afferent)
118: include system.api->                   # elements system.api depends on (efferent)
119: ```
120: 
121: Combine with `&&` (AND) and `||` (OR):
122: 
123: ```dsl
124: include element.type==Container && element.tag!=External
125: ```
126: 
127: Relationship expressions:
128: 
129: ```dsl
130: include * -> *                         # all relationships between included elements
131: include user -> *                      # all relationships from user
132: include * -> system.db                 # all relationships to database
133: include relationship.tag==Async
134: include relationship==system.api->system.db
135: ```
136: 
137: The reluctant wildcard includes everything `*` does, minus orphaned
138: elements (elements with no relationships in the view):
139: 
140: ```dsl
141: include *?
142: ```
143: 
144: `exclude` takes the same expressions.
145: 
146: ## Styles
147: 
148: ### Element Styles
149: 
150: ```dsl
151: styles {
152:     element <tag> {
153:         shape <shape>                  # see shapes below
154:         icon <file|url>
155:         width <int>
156:         height <int>
157:         background <#rrggbb>
158:         color <#rrggbb>               # text color (alias: colour)
159:         stroke <#rrggbb>              # border color
160:         strokeWidth <1-10>
161:         fontSize <int>
162:         border <solid|dashed|dotted>
163:         opacity <0-100>
164:         metadata <true|false>          # show/hide metadata line
165:         description <true|false>       # show/hide description
166:     }
167: }
168: ```
169: 
170: **Shapes**: `Box`, `RoundedBox`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Hexagon`,
171: `Diamond`, `Cylinder`, `Pipe`, `Person`, `Robot`, `Folder`,
172: `WebBrowser`, `Window`, `Terminal`, `MobileDevicePortrait`,
173: `MobileDeviceLandscape`, `Component`
174: 
175: ### Relationship Styles
176: 
177: ```dsl
178: styles {
179:     relationship <tag> {
180:         thickness <int>
181:         color <#rrggbb>
182:         style <solid|dashed|dotted>
183:         routing <Direct|Orthogonal|Curved>
184:         fontSize <int>
185:         width <int>
186:         position <0-100>               # label position along line
187:         opacity <0-100>
188:     }
189: }
190: ```
191: 
192: ### Styling All Elements/Relationships
193: 
194: Use the default tags:
195: 
196: ```dsl
197: styles {
198:     element "Element" { ... }           # applies to ALL elements
199:     relationship "Relationship" { ... } # applies to ALL relationships
200: }
201: ```
202: 
203: ### Light/Dark Mode
204: 
205: ```dsl
206: styles {
207:     light {
208:         element "Person" { background #08427B; color #ffffff }
209:     }
210:     dark {
211:         element "Person" { background #1a6bc4; color #ffffff }
212:     }
213: }
214: ```
215: 
216: ### Standard Style Recipe
217: 
218: ```dsl
219: styles {
220:     element "Person" {
221:         shape Person
222:         background #08427B
223:         color #ffffff
224:     }
225:     element "Software System" {
226:         background #1168BD
227:         color #ffffff
228:     }
229:     element "External" {
230:         background #999999
231:         color #ffffff
232:     }
233:     element "Container" {
234:         background #438DD5
235:         color #ffffff
236:     }
237:     element "Component" {
238:         background #85BBF0
239:         color #000000
240:     }
241:     element "Database" {
242:         shape Cylinder
243:     }
244:     element "Web" {
245:         shape WebBrowser
246:     }
247:     element "Queue" {
248:         shape Pipe
249:     }
250:     relationship "Relationship" {
251:         routing Orthogonal
252:     }
253:     relationship "Async" {
254:         style dashed
255:     }
256: }
257: ```
258: 
259: ## Themes
260: 
261: ```dsl
262: views {
263:     theme default                      # Structurizr default theme
264: }
265: ```
266: 
267: Built-in cloud themes (by name, no URL needed):
268: `amazon-web-services-2020.04.30`, `microsoft-azure-2021.01.26`,
269: `google-cloud-platform`, `kubernetes`. Custom styles override theme
270: defaults. Never reference a theme by URL — offline validation cannot
271: fetch it.
272: 
273: ## Terminology
274: 
275: Customize C4 terminology for your organization:
276: 
277: ```dsl
278: views {
279:     terminology {
280:         person "Actor"
281:         softwareSystem "Application"
282:         container "Service"
283:         component "Module"
284:         deploymentNode "Server"
285:         relationship "Dependency"
286:     }
287: }
288: ```
289: 
290: ## Configuration
291: 
292: ```dsl
293: configuration {
294:     scope <landscape|softwaresystem|none>
295:     visibility <private|public>
296:     users {
297:         "user@example.com" read
298:         "admin@example.com" write
299:     }
300: }
301: ```
302: 
303: ## Directives for existing elements
304: 
305: Modify elements or relationships defined elsewhere:
306: 
307: ```dsl
308: !element <identifier> {
309:     description "Updated description"
310:     tags "NewTag"
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: Bulk operations:
315: 
316: ```dsl
317: !elements element.tag==Container {
318:     tags "Monitored"
319:     properties { "team" "platform" }
320: }
321: 
322: !relationships relationship.tag==Async {
323:     tags "EventDriven"
324: }
325: ```
326: 
327: ## Common patterns
328: 
329: ### Tagging for Filtered Views
330: 
331: ```dsl
332: model {
333:     system = softwareSystem "System" {
334:         api = container "API" "REST API" "Go" "Service,v2"
335:         legacyApi = container "Legacy API" "Old REST API" "Java" "Service,v1,Deprecated"
336:     }
337: }
338: views {
339:     container system "AllContainers" { include * }
340:     filtered "AllContainers" exclude "Deprecated" "CurrentContainers"
341: }
342: ```
343: 
344: ### Async/Sync Relationship Distinction
345: 
346: ```dsl
347: model {
348:     system.api -> system.db "queries" "SQL"
349:     system.api -> system.queue "publishes order events to" "AMQP" "Async"
350:     system.worker -> system.queue "consumes order events from" "AMQP" "Async"
351: }
352: views {
353:     styles {
354:         relationship "Async" { style dashed }
355:     }
356: }
357: ```

61:     <source> -> <destination> [description] [technology]
62:     <source> -> <destination> [description] [technology]
63:     autoLayout
64:     title "Feature Y Flow"
65: }
66: ```
67: 
68: Interactions are automatically numbered in order. To set explicit
69: ordering:
70: 
71: ```dsl
72: dynamic <scope> [key] [description] {
73:     1: user -> system.api "submits order" "HTTPS"
74:     2: system.api -> system.db "persists order" "SQL"
75:     3: system.api -> system.queue "publishes event" "AMQP"
76: }
77: ```
78: 
79: ### Deployment View
80: 
81: ```dsl
82: deployment <systemId|*> <environment> [key] [description] {
83:     include *
84:     autoLayout
85:     title "Production Deployment"
86: }
87: ```
88: 
89: ### Filtered View
90: 
91: ```dsl
92: filtered <baseViewKey> <include|exclude> <tags> [key] [description]
93: ```
94: 
95: Creates a view on top of another, filtering elements by tags. The base
96: view is hidden when a filtered view exists.
97: 
98: ### AutoLayout
99: 
100: ```dsl
101: autoLayout [direction] [rankSeparation] [nodeSeparation]
102: # direction: tb (default), bt, lr, rl
103: # default separations: 300px each
104: ```
105: 
106: ### Include/Exclude with Expressions
107: 
108: Element expressions:
109: 
110: ```dsl
111: include element.type==Container
112: include element.tag==Database
113: include element.tag!=External
114: include element.parent==<id>
115: include element.technology==PostgreSQL
116: include ->system.api->                 # elements connected to system.api (both directions)
117: include ->system.api                   # elements that depend on system.api (afferent)
118: include system.api->                   # elements system.api depends on (efferent)
119: ```
120: 
121: Combine with `&&` (AND) and `||` (OR):
122: 
123: ```dsl
124: include element.type==Container && element.tag!=External
125: ```
126: 
127: Relationship expressions:
128: 
129: ```dsl
130: include * -> *                         # all relationships between included elements
131: include user -> *                      # all relationships from user
132: include * -> system.db                 # all relationships to database
133: include relationship.tag==Async
134: include relationship==system.api->system.db
135: ```
136: 
137: The reluctant wildcard includes everything `*` does, minus orphaned
138: elements (elements with no relationships in the view):
139: 
140: ```dsl
141: include *?
142: ```
143: 
144: `exclude` takes the same expressions.
145: 
146: ## Styles
147: 
148: ### Element Styles
149: 
150: ```dsl
151: styles {
152:     element <tag> {
153:         shape <shape>                  # see shapes below
154:         icon <file|url>
155:         width <int>
156:         height <int>
157:         background <#rrggbb>
158:         color <#rrggbb>               # text color (alias: colour)
159:         stroke <#rrggbb>              # border color
160:         strokeWidth <1-10>
161:         fontSize <int>
162:         border <solid|dashed|dotted>
163:         opacity <0-100>
164:         metadata <true|false>          # show/hide metadata line
165:         description <true|false>       # show/hide description
166:     }
167: }
168: ```
169: 
170: **Shapes**: `Box`, `RoundedBox`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Hexagon`,
171: `Diamond`, `Cylinder`, `Pipe`, `Person`, `Robot`, `Folder`,
172: `WebBrowser`, `Window`, `Terminal`, `MobileDevicePortrait`,
173: `MobileDeviceLandscape`, `Component`
174: 
175: ### Relationship Styles
176: 
177: ```dsl
178: styles {
179:     relationship <tag> {
180:         thickness <int>
181:         color <#rrggbb>
182:         style <solid|dashed|dotted>
183:         routing <Direct|Orthogonal|Curved>
184:         fontSize <int>
185:         width <int>
186:         position <0-100>               # label position along line
187:         opacity <0-100>
188:     }
189: }
190: ```
191: 
192: ### Styling All Elements/Relationships
193: 
194: Use the default tags:
195: 
196: ```dsl
197: styles {
198:     element "Element" { ... }           # applies to ALL elements
199:     relationship "Relationship" { ... } # applies to ALL relationships
200: }
201: ```
202: 
203: ### Light/Dark Mode
204: 
205: ```dsl
206: styles {
207:     light {
208:         element "Person" { background #08427B; color #ffffff }
209:     }
210:     dark {
211:         element "Person" { background #1a6bc4; color #ffffff }
212:     }
213: }
214: ```
215: 
216: ### Standard Style Recipe
217: 
218: ```dsl
219: styles {
220:     element "Person" {
221:         shape Person
222:         background #08427B
223:         color #ffffff
224:     }
225:     element "Software System" {
226:         background #1168BD
227:         color #ffffff
228:     }
229:     element "External" {
230:         background #999999
231:         color #ffffff
232:     }
233:     element "Container" {
234:         background #438DD5
235:         color #ffffff
236:     }
237:     element "Component" {
238:         background #85BBF0
239:         color #000000
240:     }
241:     element "Database" {
242:         shape Cylinder
243:     }
244:     element "Web" {
245:         shape WebBrowser
246:     }
247:     element "Queue" {
248:         shape Pipe
249:     }
250:     relationship "Relationship" {
251:         routing Orthogonal
252:     }
253:     relationship "Async" {
254:         style dashed
255:     }
256: }
257: ```
258: 
259: ## Themes
260: 
261: ```dsl
262: views {
263:     theme default                      # Structurizr default theme
264: }
265: ```
266: 
267: Built-in cloud themes (by name, no URL needed):
268: `amazon-web-services-2020.04.30`, `microsoft-azure-2021.01.26`,
269: `google-cloud-platform`, `kubernetes`. Custom styles override theme
270: defaults. Never reference a theme by URL — offline validation cannot
271: fetch it.
272: 
273: ## Terminology
274: 
275: Customize C4 terminology for your organization:
276: 
277: ```dsl
278: views {
279:     terminology {
280:         person "Actor"
281:         softwareSystem "Application"
282:         container "Service"
283:         component "Module"
284:         deploymentNode "Server"
285:         relationship "Dependency"
286:     }
287: }
288: ```
289: 
290: ## Configuration
291: 
292: ```dsl
293: configuration {
294:     scope <landscape|softwaresystem|none>
295:     visibility <private|public>
296:     users {
297:         "user@example.com" read
298:         "admin@example.com" write
299:     }
300: }
301: ```
302: 
303: ## Directives for existing elements
304: 
305: Modify elements or relationships defined elsewhere:
306: 
307: ```dsl
308: !element <identifier> {
309:     description "Updated description"
310:     tags "NewTag"
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: Bulk operations:
315: 
316: ```dsl
317: !elements element.tag==Container {
318:     tags "Monitored"
319:     properties { "team" "platform" }
320: }
321: 
322: !relationships relationship.tag==Async {
323:     tags "EventDriven"
324: }
325: ```
326: 
327: ## Common patterns
328: 
329: ### Tagging for Filtered Views
330: 
331: ```dsl
332: model {
333:     system = softwareSystem "System" {
334:         api = container "API" "REST API" "Go" "Service,v2"
335:         legacyApi = container "Legacy API" "Old REST API" "Java" "Service,v1,Deprecated"
336:     }
337: }
338: views {
339:     container system "AllContainers" { include * }
340:     filtered "AllContainers" exclude "Deprecated" "CurrentContainers"
341: }
342: ```
343: 
344: ### Async/Sync Relationship Distinction
345: 
346: ```dsl
347: model {
348:     system.api -> system.db "queries" "SQL"
349:     system.api -> system.queue "publishes order events to" "AMQP" "Async"
350:     system.worker -> system.queue "consumes order events from" "AMQP" "Async"
351: }
352: views {
353:     styles {
354:         relationship "Async" { style dashed }
355:     }
356: }
357: ```

# Order Management System

## Overview

The Order Management System (OMS) manages the order lifecycle from placement
to dispatch. Customers place orders through a web application; the API
orchestrates payment authorisation, persistence, and asynchronous stock
reservation.

## Key decisions

- **Synchronous payment, asynchronous fulfilment.** Payment is authorised
  inline so the customer gets immediate feedback, while stock reservation and
  dispatch run on a background worker driven by the message queue.
- **PostgreSQL as the system of record.** Orders and order lines are persisted
  in a single relational database.

## External dependencies

- **Payment Gateway** — third-party card authorisation and capture.
- **Inventory System** — stock levels across warehouses.

## Diagrams

- `SystemLandscape` — all systems and people in the domain.
- `SystemContext` — the OMS and its actors.
- `Containers` — containers within the OMS.
- `ApiComponents` — components within the API.
- `PlaceOrder` — the end-to-end order placement flow.
- `Production` — the production deployment.

## What I set up in `/work`

```

`workspace.dsl` pulls the fragments together with `!include` (inside `model { }` and `views { }`) and points at the docs folder with `!docs docs`.

## Verification with the structurizr MCP tools

The MCP tools **refuse `!include`, `!docs`, and `!adrs`** (the filesystem/documentation feature flags aren't enabled), so they can't parse the multi-file layout directly. I verified the **inlined single-file equivalent** — the same workspace with every `!include` resolved to its file's content and the `!docs` line stripped (built with a small `awk` splice, saved at `/tmp/inlined.dsl`):

- **`inspect`** → two remaining findings:
  - `The software system "Order Management System" has containers, but is missing documentation.`
  - `... is missing decisions.`

I fixed the third finding (no workspace scope) by adding `configuration { scope softwareSystem }`. The two above can't be cleared through the MCP because they require `!docs`/`!adrs` directives **on the system**, which the MCP refuses by design.

## Notes / caveats

- The `!include` and `!docs` directives themselves follow standard Structurizr DSL syntax, but the MCP can't check them (it rejects them) — what the MCP *did* check is the fully inlined model, which validates.
- If you want to silence those two `inspect` findings in the real workspace, add `!docs docs/oms` and `!adrs adrs/oms` inside the `oms = softwareSystem { ... }` block in `model/order-management.dsl` (the team's actual Structurizr tooling supports this; only the MCP here doesn't).
- I dropped a deployment view/nodes: this DSL build doesn't accept `deploymentNode` at model level (it wants `deploymentEnvironment`, whose syntax isn't documented in the available references), so I didn't guess at it. Easy to add back if you tell me the deployment syntax your tooling uses.
